html:
SMTO-PSM-0012 — A parameter's value or context isn't in the right shape

GUID: e70e45c1-761f-4076-a0b8-e920efd63c35
Slug: parameter-context-invalid
Domain: PSM · Subsystem: psm

What happened

  • SMTO tried to save a parameter, but its value or its context wasn't a list of named fields as SMTO requires. The parameter was not saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Parameter Store, open the parameter, go to the Value tab and make sure the value is written as named fields inside curly braces, for example {"host": "server1"}. SMTO stores each parameter as a set of named fields, and a bare word, number or list is rejected.
  2. If you just want to store a piece of text, select FREE FORM above the value box, type the text, then select Save. FREE FORM wraps your text in the right shape for you, so you don't have to write named fields.
  3. If the Agent was saving the parameter for you, tell it the field names and values you want, for example "save @my_server with host server1 and port 443". This error happens when the Agent sends the value in the wrong shape, and naming the fields lets it send them correctly.

What success looks like

  • Parameter Store shows Saved, and the parameter appears in the list.

If it still fails

  • Don't keep resending the same value. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, without including any passwords.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Parameter create/update validation received a non-object context_json, or parameters.manage create received a value_json that is not a non-empty object.

What this means

  • Context create/update validation receives a non-object, or the management tool receives a non-object value_json. Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.

Why this can happen

  • Context create/update validation receives a non-object, or the management tool receives a non-object value_json.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify whether the rejected field is context_json or management value_json before editing it.

How to fix it

  • Send value_json and context_json as JSON objects ({...}); value_json must also be non-empty for create. The messages come from AgentParameterCreate/AgentParameterUpdate validators in src/agent_runtime/parameters/models.py and RuntimeManageParameterStoreCapability.execute in src/agent_runtime/skills/parameters/tools.py.
  • Supply a JSON object for the rejected field and follow that field's separate emptiness constraints.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact field validates as an object under its operation's schema.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Accepted parameter bindings preserve exact identity and revision. Validation does not authorize secret substitution, alias guessing or replay of earlier work; failed write confirmation requires reading the original stored state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
